title: Metric enrichment mismatch: K8s annotations lost in metrics pipeline causing autoscaler under-provisioning
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated customers observed sustained tail latency and request shedding during 2026-03-09 18:00-20:00 UTC. We traced root cause to the autoscaler under-counting active tenant demand because the metric enrichment service dropped k8s pod tenant annotations for ~30% of pods in two AZs. The autoscaler therefore believed there was sufficient headroom and did not scale reserved pools or burst capacity, causing reserved pool exhaustion and tail latency increases for affected tenants.

Scope: Impacted Dedicated clusters in us-east-1a and us-east-1b; ~12 medium/large tenants saw failed burst admission or elevated 95/99th latency. Hosted customers unaffected. Private agents in some customer VPCs also reported similar missing annotation telemetry but did not mismatch because private autoscaler used a different tagging fallback.

Root cause: A schema migration in the metrics enrichment pipeline (metric-enricher v3.2.0) introduced a new binary header that caused an upstream sidecar to skip copying k8s annotations on spool rotation. The enrichment step that maps pod -> tenant_id silently emitted a metric with an empty tenant label rather than failing, so autoscaler aggregated it under the default bucket.

Immediate mitigation (done): 1) Reverted metric-enricher to v3.1.8 in affected regions (hotfix rollout completed by 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC). 2) Re-enabled a fallback in the autoscaler to use allocation leases when tenant label is missing (short-term guard). 3) Issued customer comms and opened dedicated support tickets for top 10 impacted customers.

Permanent fix (in flight): Patch metric-enricher to validate annotation copy and fail loudly on schema mismatch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metric-enricher/pull/1287). Add end-to-end test for spool rotation+annotation preservation. Improve autoscaler to: a) raise a telemetry alert when >1% of requests have missing tenant labels for >5m, b) fallback to conservative scaling policy when tenant label entropy is low.

Acceptance criteria: 1) metric-enricher change merged and rolled to staging + canary; 2) autoscaler fallback retained until telemetry shows <0.1% label loss for 24h; 3) runbook updated and teams trained on procedure; 4) follow-up postmortem published with customer remediation notes.
